_schema: entry_id -> { cat: creature|item|place, title, body, hint }. Logs come from readables.json at runtime.

creature_gull.title: Gulls
creature_gull.body: Still here, wheeling around the high iron. They go at dusk, all of them at once. Whatever clock they run on, it hasn't been interrupted.
creature_gull.hint: Follow their lead: when the gulls go, get to the light.

creature_jelly_drifter.title: Jelly Drifters
creature_jelly_drifter.body: After dark the water fills with slow teal bells, pulsing as they turn around the rig. They keep off the legs. I watched them for an hour and lost the time.
creature_jelly_drifter.hint: They only surface at night. Whatever they feed on rises then too.

creature_barnacle.title: Lamp Barnacles
creature_barnacle.body: Growths on the legs at the waterline. They glow at night until I get close, then they don't. They feel me coming through the steel.
creature_barnacle.hint: If the barnacles go dark and I haven't moved… something else is on the steel.

creature_lamp_eel.title: Lamp-Eel
creature_lamp_eel.body: A chain of light doing figure-eights off the north edge, bright at the head, fading down its length. Same route every time. I can't tell if it's hunting or just going round.
creature_lamp_eel.hint: It surfaces at full dark, north side. Best view from the pontoon or the galley roof.

creature_fiddler_shoal.title: Fiddler Shoal
creature_fiddler_shoal.body: Small quick fish schooling under the wet deck lip. Silver in daylight. At dusk they take a teal glint off the Bloom. Gone by full dark.
creature_fiddler_shoal.hint: They hide when night comes. Smart fish. Consider imitating the fish.

creature_mantle_ray.title: The Mantle
creature_mantle_ray.body: Something crossed over the rig in the dark. Wide flat wings, underside speckled with light, a noise like a hull settling. It didn't circle. Straight over and gone.
creature_mantle_ray.hint: The chalk tally on the bunkhouse roof counts something. I think it counts this.

creature_tide_worm.title: Tide Worms
creature_tide_worm.body: Finger-length worms up out of the deck drains at dawn and dusk, teal at the tips, swaying. Footsteps put them back down. They've never done anything to me.
creature_tide_worm.hint: They keep tide hours: dawn and dusk only.

creature_lamplight_crab.title: The Giant Crab
creature_lamplight_crab.body: Dog-sized, blue-shelled, claws up like bolt cutters. Daylight they hold below the waterline; lean over the east rim and you can watch them work along the pontoon faces. After dark they come up over the edge and walk the plate. They won't cross powered light and a beam held on one turns it round. In the dark that claw takes a piece out of you.
creature_lamplight_crab.hint: Daylight: look over the east deck edge. Night: keep to the lit decks, keep a torch in hand, and if one closes — run; they quit a chase you outrun.

creature_glow_worm.title: Glow Worms
creature_glow_worm.body: A knuckle of teal in the dark corners. Under the stair, against the leg bases, never the same corner twice. It reads footsteps through the plate and drops into its den before I'm near. Went in slow one night and got a hand round one. Mostly light and muscle.
creature_glow_worm.hint: Crouch to close the last few meters. Sear it at the bench before eating — raw ones bite back.

creature_epic_whale.title: The Four-Eyed
creature_epic_whale.body: It came over higher than the mast. Body like a hull, too many fins all rowing out of time, four eyes burning teal down its back. Swimming the night air the way a thing swims water. I stood and watched. It never looked down.
creature_epic_whale.hint: Full dark, high up, rare. When the long groan comes and the crab isn't moving — look up.

item_canned_food.title: Canned Food
item_canned_food.body: Meridian mess stock. Dented, no label. Fine.
item_canned_food.hint: Eat from the hotbar (1–4). Restores a good meal's worth of hunger.

item_canned_peaches.title: Canned Peaches
item_canned_peaches.body: Somebody was hoarding these behind the flour. I'd have done the same.
item_canned_peaches.hint: Eat from the hotbar. Lighter than a full can of stew.

item_water_ration.title: Water Ration
item_water_ration.body: SPHL survival stock. Foil pouch. Tastes of the bag.

item_sealed_tin.title: Sealed Tin
item_sealed_tin.body: Came out of the gyre still watertight. Cold all the way through.
item_sealed_tin.hint: Eat from the hotbar. The gyre keeps bringing them — keep the hook handy.

item_kelp_bundle.title: Kelp Bundle
item_kelp_bundle.body: Bloom-touched kelp, faint glow to it. The old crew's notes say it's safe to eat, and the old crew isn't here to ask. I've had it three times now with no trouble.
item_kelp_bundle.hint: Edible, small — or bench it: 2× kelp + scrap → bloom lamp. Light the crab honors.

item_cable_spool.title: Cable Spool
item_cable_spool.body: Marine-grade, enough on the drum to splice a burned run.
item_cable_spool.hint: Take it to the burned cable gap in Breaker Room 4-A, then throw the breaker.

item_prybar.title: Prybar
item_prybar.body: Bent iron. The pump room gave it up without much of a fight.
item_prybar.hint: Craftable: lash it to a rope coil at the rigging bench → throwing hook.

item_rope.title: Rope Coil
item_rope.body: Salt-stiff but sound. Riggers put their weight on this stuff.
item_rope.hint: Craftable: rope + prybar at the wet-deck rigging bench → throwing hook.

item_throwing_hook.title: Throwing Hook
item_throwing_hook.body: A heaving line with teeth on the end. The gyre collects what the sea takes and this is how I get it back.
item_throwing_hook.hint: Press F to throw. It combs the surface on the way back — aim past what you want.

item_flare.title: Flare
item_flare.hint: No striker yet. There'll be a use for this. (v0.2)

item_life_ring.title: Life Ring
item_life_ring.body: Cork and canvas. RIG 4 SLIPWAY stencilled on it, most of it worn off.
item_life_ring.hint: If something goes in the water that shouldn't… this is the answer. (v0.2)

item_driftwood.title: Driftwood Plank
item_driftwood.body: Ship-cut lumber gone smooth. Not off this rig. Came from somewhere further down the line.
item_driftwood.hint: Bench recipes: 2× driftwood → walkway · with tarp → lean-to · with scrap → barricade.

item_scrap_metal.title: Scrap Metal
item_scrap_metal.body: Plate fragments, paint still on one side. Same grey as our rails.
item_scrap_metal.hint: Bench recipes: with 2× kelp → bloom lamp · 2× scrap + driftwood → barricade.

item_tarp.title: Canvas Tarp
item_tarp.body: Heavy weather canvas, whole, hems intact. Folds down to nothing.
item_tarp.hint: Bench recipe: tarp + 2× driftwood → lean-to. A pocket of warmth anywhere.

place_sphl.title: The SPHL
place_sphl.body: Six days sealed in an orange pressure pod while the machine gave my blood back to the surface. It kept me alive without a word of comment. Hatch is open now. I still sleep in it.
place_sphl.hint: If the night goes wrong, I wake up here. It counts as 'going wrong'.

place_gyre.title: The Gyre
place_gyre.body: The current south of the rig turns in a slow circle and everything the sea is carrying ends up turning with it. Wood, rope, tins, kelp. At night the Bloom gathers under the eye of it.
place_gyre.hint: Everything spirals to the middle. A thrown hook crosses the whole eye on the reel-in.

place_rigging_bench.title: The Rigging Bench
place_rigging_bench.body: A work-worn bench on the wet deck. Lay parts out on it and it shows you what they'll make. Then you do the hammering yourself.
place_rigging_bench.hint: Known so far: throwing hook, bloom lamp, lean-to, walkway, barricade. New parts may know new shapes.

place_fire_barrel.title: The Fire Barrel
place_fire_barrel.body: A drum of coals somebody kept going on the wet deck. I keep it going now. It doesn't need the grid.
place_fire_barrel.hint: Stand close to drive the cold out — the sea soaks into your bones down here.

place_power.title: The Grid
place_power.body: Spliced the burned run, threw Master 4-A, and the floodlights came up with a hum. First proper light on this rig since the Flash.
place_power.hint: The circuit holds the topside floodlights. What walks at night won't cross their wash.

item_bloom_lamp_kit.title: Bloom Lamp (kit)
item_bloom_lamp_kit.body: Kelp sealed in a scrap housing, ready to raise. Cold teal light, no breaker and no cable behind it.
item_bloom_lamp_kit.hint: Press B to build. Place them along the paths you'll need after dark. The crab honors their light.

item_leanto_kit.title: Lean-To (kit)
item_leanto_kit.body: Canvas over driftwood, folded flat and lashed for carrying.
item_leanto_kit.hint: Press B to build. A pocket of warmth anywhere on the rig — no grid required.

item_walkway_kit.title: Plank Walkway (kit)
item_walkway_kit.body: A lashed plank section. Puts deck where the rig hasn't got any.
item_walkway_kit.hint: Press B to build. Bridges gaps, extends decks, makes paths.

item_barricade_kit.title: Barricade (kit)
item_barricade_kit.body: Scrap plate on a wood brace. Waist-high and heavy enough.
item_barricade_kit.hint: Press B to build. Cover, wind-break, or just a wall where I want a wall.

place_building.title: Building
place_building.body: Raised something on this rig with my own hands. Wasn't here yesterday. The rig doesn't seem to mind.
place_building.hint: Craft kits at the bench → B for build mode → LMB places, R rotates, Tab cycles kits.

creature_seal.title: Harbor Seal
creature_seal.body: One hauled out on the wet deck this morning and watched me the whole time I worked. No fear in it at all. Twelve years ago it would have gone straight back in. This one just looked, and kept looking.
creature_seal.hint: They herd fish toward a still net. Earn one's trust and you never fish alone.

creature_lamp_snail.title: Lamp Snails
creature_lamp_snail.body: Lean over the rail on a dark night and the legs are wearing lamps. Shells the size of a wheelbarrow with cold light running through them in veins. They go round the waterline at a crawl and the whole platform stands in that glow after sundown.
creature_lamp_snail.hint: On an outgoing tide some strand on the leg bracing. A gentle harvest takes the glow-mucus and leaves the animal.

fish_herring.title: Lantern Herring
fish_herring.body: The shoal glows. You can net them at night by their own light, which feels like cheating and isn't.
fish_herring.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_slate_cod.title: Slate Cod
fish_slate_cod.body: Heavy, slow, scales like roofing slate. Fought like a wet sandbag. Still glad of it.
fish_slate_cod.hint: Bites: day · storms help · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_mirrorjack.title: Mirrorjack
fish_mirrorjack.body: Chrome flanks. It threw the dawn back at me hard enough that I nearly lost the rod over the rail.
fish_mirrorjack.hint: Bites: dawn/dusk · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

fish_chimefish.title: Chimefish
fish_chimefish.body: It rang against the rail when I lifted it clear. Rang, like a struck glass. I've no explanation.
fish_chimefish.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · calm seas only · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_sable_hake.title: Sable Hake
fish_sable_hake.body: They come up to worklight after dark. The floodlit rail is a fishing spot now.
fish_sable_hake.hint: Bites: night · close to the rig · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_barrel_grouper.title: Goliath Grouper
fish_barrel_grouper.body: Bloom-big. Feeds a week and my arms will remember it for longer.
fish_barrel_grouper.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · storms help · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Prime Fillet

fish_ribbon_eel.title: Ribbon Eel
fish_ribbon_eel.body: Came up crackling with a faint charge and the line tasted of storm. Handle it with gloves.
fish_ribbon_eel.hint: Bites: night · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Prime Fillet

fish_the_looker.title: The Looker
fish_the_looker.body: Had it at the rail. It looked back at me, and I had my hands open before I'd decided anything.
fish_the_looker.hint: Ultra-rare. It is never kept. It was never going to be kept.

system_fishing.title: Fishing
system_fishing.body: The rod out of the storeroom works. Cast to open water, watch the float, strike when it dips. After that it's give and take: reel when the line slacks, rest when it screams.
system_fishing.hint: Hold LMB to reel, ease off before the tension bar tops out.

system_drop_net.title: The Drop Net
system_drop_net.body: Rope and driftwood. Lower it, go and do something else, come back to breakfast.
system_drop_net.hint: Soaks best through dusk and dark.

system_stove.title: The Galley Stove
system_stove.body: The old range still holds pressure in its bottle. Seared fish, hot pan. The galley smelled like a galley again.
system_stove.hint: COOK at the stove turns raw catch into a real meal.

item_fishing_rod.title: Fishing Rod
item_fishing_rod.body: A rigger's rod out of the storeroom, cork grip worn to the shape of someone else's hands.
item_fishing_rod.hint: Select it on the hotbar; LMB casts to open water.

item_drop_net_kit.title: Drop Net
item_drop_net_kit.body: Rope and driftwood. The rig can fish while I sleep.
item_drop_net_kit.hint: Place it at a deck edge — it needs open water below.

item_cooked_fish.title: Seared Fish
item_cooked_fish.hint: Eat from the hotbar. Beats canned everything.

item_cooked_fish_prime.title: Prime Fillet
item_cooked_fish_prime.body: The big deep ones render down rich. A proper meal, the sort you sit down for.
item_cooked_fish_prime.hint: The grouper and the eel sear into this.

item_fish_herring.title: Lantern Herring (raw)
item_fish_herring.body: Glows faintly even out of the water.
item_fish_herring.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

item_fish_slate_cod.title: Slate Cod (raw)
item_fish_slate_cod.body: Heavy as the name. Scales like roof slate.

item_fish_chimefish.title: Chimefish (raw)
item_fish_chimefish.body: It rang when it came over the rail.

item_fish_sable_hake.title: Sable Hake (raw)
item_fish_sable_hake.body: Comes up to worklight. The floodlit rail fishes best after dark.

fish_copper_sprat.title: Copper Sprat
fish_copper_sprat.body: Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. Not worth eating, worth keeping.
fish_copper_sprat.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_copper_sprat.title: Copper Sprat (raw)
item_fish_copper_sprat.body: Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. Not worth eating, worth keeping.
item_fish_copper_sprat.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_silver_ladder.title: Silver Ladder
fish_silver_ladder.body: Dawn columns over open water. The shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar of them.
fish_silver_ladder.hint: Bites: dawn · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_silver_ladder.title: Silver Ladder (raw)
item_fish_silver_ladder.body: Dawn columns over open water. The shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar of them.
item_fish_silver_ladder.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_ember_snapper.title: Ember Snapper
fish_ember_snapper.body: Warm-bodied. Crowds the outfalls and any steel the rig has been heating. Fish the deck shadow.
fish_ember_snapper.hint: Bites: day/dusk · close to the rig · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_ember_snapper.title: Ember Snapper (raw)
item_fish_ember_snapper.body: Warm-bodied. Crowds the outfalls and any steel the rig has been heating. Fish the deck shadow.
item_fish_ember_snapper.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_ghost_sole.title: Ghost Sole
fish_ghost_sole.body: Near-invisible in daylight. Night water near a glow is where it shows up.
fish_ghost_sole.hint: Bites: night · close to the rig · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_ghost_sole.title: Ghost Sole (raw)
item_fish_ghost_sole.body: Near-invisible in daylight. Night water near a glow is where it shows up.
item_fish_ghost_sole.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_glasspike.title: Glasspike
fish_glasspike.body: Clear still nights, open water. A pike you can see through. You find it by the grit in its gut.
fish_glasspike.hint: Bites: night · calm seas only · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_glasspike.title: Glasspike (raw)
item_fish_glasspike.body: Clear still nights, open water. A pike you can see through. You find it by the grit in its gut.
item_fish_glasspike.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_lodestone_bream.title: Lodestone Bream
fish_lodestone_bream.body: Deep daylight water. Its bones are magnetised and spin a compass needle right round.
fish_lodestone_bream.hint: Bites: day · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_lodestone_bream.title: Lodestone Bream (raw)
item_fish_lodestone_bream.body: Deep daylight water. Its bones are magnetised and spin a compass needle right round.
item_fish_lodestone_bream.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_drum_croaker.title: Drum Croaker
fish_drum_croaker.body: Storm fish. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes in, and then they bite hard.
fish_drum_croaker.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · storms ONLY · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_drum_croaker.title: Drum Croaker (raw)
item_fish_drum_croaker.body: Storm fish. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes in, and then they bite hard.
item_fish_drum_croaker.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_inkwell_squid.title: Inkwell Squid
fish_inkwell_squid.body: Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink.
fish_inkwell_squid.hint: Bites: night · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_inkwell_squid.title: Inkwell Squid (raw)
item_fish_inkwell_squid.body: Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink.
item_fish_inkwell_squid.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_stone_crab.title: Stone Crab
fish_stone_crab.body: Walks into a soaked net and never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard.
fish_stone_crab.hint: Bites: dusk/night · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_stone_crab.title: Stone Crab (raw)
item_fish_stone_crab.body: Walks into a soaked net and never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard.
item_fish_stone_crab.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_gutter_prawn.title: Gutter Prawn
fish_gutter_prawn.body: Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few in it.
fish_gutter_prawn.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_gutter_prawn.title: Gutter Prawn (raw)
item_fish_gutter_prawn.body: Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few in it.
item_fish_gutter_prawn.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_miller_flounder.title: Miller's Flounder
fish_miller_flounder.body: Deck-plate camouflage and bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them in daylight.
fish_miller_flounder.hint: Bites: day · close to the rig · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_miller_flounder.title: Miller's Flounder (raw)
item_fish_miller_flounder.body: Deck-plate camouflage and bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them in daylight.
item_fish_miller_flounder.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_fathom_halibut.title: Fathom Halibut
fish_fathom_halibut.body: Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up and the winch complains about it. Feeds a week.
fish_fathom_halibut.hint: Bites: night · takes: net · sears to Prime Fillet

item_fish_fathom_halibut.title: Fathom Halibut (raw)
item_fish_fathom_halibut.body: Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up and the winch complains about it. Feeds a week.
item_fish_fathom_halibut.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

creature_hammerhead.title: Ultra Hammerhead
creature_hammerhead.body: It came off its patrol line the moment I went under. A hammer the width of a doorway swinging through the murk to look at me with both ends of its face. Sometimes it circles. Sometimes it carries on. I don't get a say in which.
creature_hammerhead.hint: They patrol below the swell and mostly attack swimmers who come close. The deck is yours; the water is theirs.

system_preserving.title: Keeping the Catch
system_preserving.body: Raw fish turns in about four hours on the line. The fridge holds it indefinitely. Cooked fish hung up cures into dried, and dried keeps.
system_preserving.hint: HANG fish on a marked line, or STOW it in the galley fridge. Cooked + 4 hours hung = dried, keeps forever.

item_dried_fish.title: Dried Fish
item_dried_fish.body: Wind-cured on the line. Keeps indefinitely and eats like the memory of a hot meal.

item_fish_rotten.title: Rotten Fish
item_fish_rotten.body: Left too long on the line. Even the gulls have passed on it.
item_fish_rotten.hint: Eating this is a mistake you make once.

codex_what_osk_chose.title: What Osk Chose
codex_what_osk_chose.body: Four scraps in four corners of the rig, one man coming apart toward the light instead of away from it. Osk saw it first, on the derrick, the night the water learned his name. He didn't muster and he didn't take a boat. He walked down the line toward the Quiet Rig, toward whatever the company was keeping down there, because he'd decided seeing it was worth more than getting off. I keep his notes in a row now. Some nights I'm not sure he had it wrong.
codex_what_osk_chose.hint: He kept the lamps lit. So do I. It's the only prayer left that works.

codex_down_the_line.title: Down the Line
codex_down_the_line.body: Food, cable, spool stock. Whole pallets going out on the supply boat, offloaded at night with nobody on deck, all of it moving toward the platform at the end of the chain. The one they wouldn't name. The one they let the bridges rot toward. Filed as a processing terminus. Nine hundred miles from anywhere and Meridian was pouring the whole throat of the line into its far end. Processing what, is the question I keep coming back to. I think they were feeding it.
codex_down_the_line.hint: The Quiet Rig is seven bridges east. The bridges are gone. Good.

codex_the_flash.title: The Flash
codex_the_flash.body: Every gauge on the drill deck read zero in the same second. The sea lit up under leg four. The toolpusher shut the well in and nobody argued, and on this rig somebody always argues. Then the radios: the water is awake, no code for it, going dark. Whatever the company had been growing down the line finished growing all at once and the light came up out of the whole ocean. They called it the Flash because the other way of putting it won't fit in a log.
codex_the_flash.hint: It didn't end the world. It woke it. Not the same thing.

codex_the_count.title: The Count
codex_the_count.body: Somebody spent their last good nights up here with a chalk stub counting the Mantle's crossings. Thirty-one, then a gap where the counting stopped mattering, then four more gouged in deep. IT COMES BACK, underneath. I've seen it once now. It didn't circle and it didn't look down. I understand keeping the tally. It's the only calendar out here that still means anything.
codex_the_count.hint: Add your own marks. Something should still be counting.

place_davits.title: The Empty Davits
place_davits.body: Two sets of falls, both run out, both empty. Lifeboat 2 got away. The stencil says it launched full. Somebody stood right here and made the count, forty aboard and one short, and lowered away regardless, because a boat that waits is a boat that drowns. I don't hold it against them. I'd have counted the same. I'm the one that didn't fit.
place_davits.hint: The falls still work. If anything ever comes back for me, this is where it lands.

place_derrick.title: The Derrick
place_derrick.body: The drill string goes down through the floor and keeps going past anything I want to think about. The toolpusher's last log says the quiet coming back up it wasn't the quiet of a good hole. I stood on the floor one night and put my hand on the pipe. It was warm. Wells aren't warm.
place_derrick.hint: Osk saw it first from the catwalk up here. Best and worst view on the rig.

place_quiet_rig.title: Platform 7 — The Quiet Rig
place_quiet_rig.body: Seven bridges east, or where the bridges used to be. The end of the line. Where the food went and the cable went and the company grew the light and filed it as a terminus. I'll never stand on it. The sea took the bridges and won't give a boat leave to go that way. I've stopped deciding whether that's the sea keeping me off it or keeping it off me.
place_quiet_rig.hint: Everything came from down the line. The Bloom most of all.

creature_rust_snail.title: Rust Snails
creature_rust_snail.body: Follow a bright scoured line in the corrosion far enough and there's an animal at the end of it. Shell the colour of what it eats, oxide orange and banded and flaking, with a warm amber light down in the whorls. They rasp the steel. Slowly, they are taking this rig apart and wearing it.
creature_rust_snail.hint: Where the handrail has gone thin and clean, one has been working. The shell plate is rich in iron if you can get it off.

creature_glass_snail.title: Glass Snails
creature_glass_snail.body: Under the wet-deck lip, on plate that never sees sun, there's a slow teal spiral turning in the dark. The shell is glass. Actual glass. The light is its gut working. Come closer and it doesn't shrink; it burns up brighter and turns the lit coil toward you.
creature_glass_snail.hint: They brighten to a nearby lamp. Stand still and the whole underside of the deck lights up.

creature_pyramid_snail.title: Pyramid Snails
creature_pyramid_snail.body: A spire of black and white winding to a point, ringed with pale spikes on every step, riding a broad grey foot that ripples as it goes. Eyes up on stalks, and it swings them round to hold you while it keeps walking. The other three never leave the water line. This one crosses the whole topside, changes its mind about what's interesting, and goes that way instead.
creature_pyramid_snail.hint: It is going somewhere, not patrolling — wait where you are and it will come to you. Greens will stop it dead, and a fed pair will make a third.

creature_anchor_limpet.title: Anchor Limpets
creature_anchor_limpet.body: A riveted iron cap set into the splash zone with a thin band of light underneath. Walk at one and it feels you through the plate long before you arrive. The shell settles, the ring goes out, and then it's just part of the rig. Storms don't move them.
creature_anchor_limpet.hint: The light only returns if you stop moving. Patience is the whole trick with these.

system_snail_breeding.title: Feeding the Snails
system_snail_breeding.body: Kelp does it. Any lamp, rust or glass snail takes a green offering and burns a shade brighter after. Out on the SW pontoon I fed two in an evening and carried one over to sit by the other. By morning there was a third light working the same patch, small and pale. Nobody taught them that.
system_snail_breeding.hint: FEED a crawling snail a green item. Two fed snails of the same kind, brought within a few metres of each other, breed — a permanent baby, no despawn, ever.

creature_snail_baby.title: A New Light
creature_snail_baby.body: Half the size of its parents and twice as restless, already crawling its own short patch of the leg base. There are more lights on this rig than there were, and it's because I fed them.
creature_snail_baby.hint: Babies grow to full size over a couple of days. They never starve and they never vanish.

item_snail_live.title: Live Snail
item_snail_live.body: Collected whole. Shell, foot, and the last of its light going out slowly in the dark of the pack. It was crawling a minute ago.
item_snail_live.hint: Sears on the galley stove into escargot. Works on a baby the same as a grown one.

item_escargot.title: Escargot
item_escargot.body: Seared in its own shell. Small, rich, and the best thing I've eaten out here. The constellation on the leg is one light short tonight and I ate it anyway.
item_escargot.hint: Solid hunger, a little comfort besides — the pot is kinder to you than the tide ever was.

fish_skipjack_tuna.title: Skipjack Tuna
fish_skipjack_tuna.body: The small one, and never alone. They boil the surface in open water by day.

fish_yellowfin_tuna.title: Yellowfin Tuna
fish_yellowfin_tuna.body: Gold down the flank, sickle fins half its own length. Runs the moment it feels the hook.

fish_albacore_tuna.title: Albacore Tuna
fish_albacore_tuna.body: Pectorals like scythes, reaching most of the way down it. Cold water and long runs.

fish_bigeye_tuna.title: Bigeye Tuna
fish_bigeye_tuna.body: That eye is for the dark water it hunts in. Up at dusk, down again by morning.

fish_bluefin_tuna.title: Bluefin Tuna
fish_bluefin_tuna.body: The big one. A quarter tonne built like a torpedo. It will empty the spool.

fish_bluelined_grouper.title: Bluelined Grouper
fish_bluelined_grouper.body: Electric blue pinstripes on olive. Holds station in the leg shadow and waits.

fish_peacock_grouper.title: Peacock Grouper
fish_peacock_grouper.body: Covered in blue eyespots, every one ringed black.

fish_humpback_grouper.title: Humpback Grouper
fish_humpback_grouper.body: Small head on a steep white back, black spots all over. Odd-looking, slow, unbothered.

fish_leopard_grouper.title: Leopard Coral Grouper
fish_leopard_grouper.body: Coral red with electric blue spots, and quicker off the mark than a fish that size should be.

fish_mahi_mahi.title: Mahi-Mahi
fish_mahi_mahi.body: Green-gold and lit from inside, forehead like a blunt axe. Fast, and it jumps.

fish_swallowtail.title: Swallowtail Angelfish
fish_swallowtail.body: Two long filaments trailing off the tail. Barely worth eating. Worth looking at.

creature_ship_cat.title: Ship's Cat
creature_ship_cat.body: Somebody's, once. Found her washing a paw in the bunkhouse like the evacuation was a rumour she hadn't heard. She's decided about me now, and she comes along.
creature_ship_cat.hint: Found in the bunkhouse · say hello once · follows you · settles when you rest · very interested in fish · hunts the deck gulls · stretches when it wakes · gets the zoomies

cat_gift.title: The Cat Brings Something
cat_gift.body: She went low and slow across the plating with her belly a hand's width off the deck, froze twice, wound herself up on her back feet, and missed. Sat down and washed for a solid minute afterwards like she'd meant to. The next one she didn't miss. Carried the feather all the way back with her head held clear of her own paws, put it down in front of me, and waited to see what I'd do about it.
cat_gift.hint: Stalks deck gulls · misses more often than not · washes furiously when it does · brings you what it catches
